beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A low generation cost does not make those other requirements disappear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The materials chapter makes a related distinction between geological inventory and industrial supply.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mines and refineries take time even when the relevant atoms are not nearly exhausted.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Substitution and recycling can help without removing every need for new extraction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading these chapters replaces a single abundance slogan with a chain of concrete dependencies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The living world adds limits that cannot be reduced to an energy balance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Food can be plentiful in aggregate while healthy diets remain inaccessible locally.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Water for a city and water for agriculture require different scales of analysis.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Soils, watersheds, biodiversity, and climate stability constrain how productive systems can expand.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book tests optimistic possibilities against these distinctions rather than treating nature as inventory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its examples show why one technological success cannot stand in for the whole argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader gains a more precise account of which bottleneck a proposed solution addresses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Cheap digital intelligence does not instantly create reliable physical work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The robotics chapters focus on useful hours, safety, supervision, servicing, and total cost.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A striking demonstration is different from dependable operation in an ordinary household.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book compares the economic role of personal robots with the automobile.
